findings.title: Required owner decisions remain unresolved
findings.details: Issue #217 explicitly blocks implementation and release work on authenticated decisions O217-1 through O217-7. No supplied owner comment resolves them; the sole owner comment is truncated and cannot establish a complete authorization. Expected: each decision is answered by an authenticated owner signal for this exact issue version, incorporated without rewriting protected owner history, and the resulting contract is reviewed again. Result: blocked and not review-clean.

findings.title: Declared blocking dependencies are not complete
findings.details: The execution sequence requires #253 and #275 before CLI/TUI integration, while the supplied current issue records both as open; #275 also declares prerequisite work including #253 and #260. Expected: dependency state and required revisions are verified complete before implementation or release integration is admitted, with exact merged-revision evidence. Result: issue #217 is not implementation-ready.

findings.title: Route failure and fallback requirements conflict with canonical runtime ownership and verified state
findings.details: The contract correctly assigns route resolution to the canonical Agent OS runtime, but later requires unavailable logical routes to remain unavailable without fallback and says provider substitution needs O217-3. Trusted current state records canonical routing that skips unavailable providers and can resolve medium/max through Claude, while Kimi is decommissioned and Codex is temporarily blocked. O217-3 addresses only the default Kimi behavior and does not resolve this broader conflict. Expected: #217 only requests logical tier and effort and renders the runtime-returned resolution, or an authenticated owner decision changes fallback policy in the runtime-owned #253/#275 contract. Result: acceptance behavior is presently contradictory and stale.

findings.title: Signed-manifest verification remains underspecified
findings.details: O217-4 asks for signing authority, trust root, custody, rotation, and redirect policy, but neither the contract nor that owner question requires the signature algorithm, signature/envelope encoding, canonical signed-byte representation, key-identifier binding, or verifier behavior during key rotation. Those choices are necessary for deterministic cross-platform verification and negative fixtures. Expected: trusted release policy or an expanded owner decision defines these exact semantics before artifacts or updater behavior are implemented. Result: the supply-chain acceptance contract remains unverifiable even if O217-4 is answered as currently written.

findings.title: Required blocked-state label is absent
findings.details: The supplied current target lists only label P1, while trusted policy permits df:reviewed and df:ask-owner and the issue itself requires df:ask-owner while owner decisions remain open. Expected: the exact issue version carries df:ask-owner and must not carry a reviewed/ready outcome until all findings are cleared. Result: durable GitHub control-plane state does not reflect the contract's blocked status.
